key_insight: Physics-localized hyper-reduction preserves coupled soil displacement and pore-pressure predictions while accelerating elastoplastic hydro-mechanical simulations by up to 77×.
engineering_relevance: Faster repeated simulations can support calibration, uncertainty quantification and scenario analysis for partially saturated earthfill and tailings dams.
method: Build separate displacement and pore-pressure reduced bases using proper orthogonal decomposition.
Evaluate affine residual terms exactly and approximate nonlinear corrections using one ECSW cubature rule per balance equation.
Assemble the original FEniCSx variational forms only on ECSW-selected elements.
evidence_signal: Tests on 2D and 3D dams undergoing raising and consolidation, with varying material parameters and raise height, reported field errors below 0.5% relative to finite elements and speed-ups up to 43× and 77×, respectively.
watch_item: Accuracy beyond the tested parameter ranges and loading scenarios remains unestablished; new yielding or unsaturated zones may require updated training and element selection.
paper_title: A hyper-reduction strategy for elastoplastic hydro-mechanical problems in partially saturated soil
